title: Stream Guardian: Reconnect Orchestrator and Fragment Coherence for SSE Clients
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a client-server reconnect orchestration (Stream Guardian) for SSE that provides fragment coherence, idempotent resume, function-call boundary safety, and a lightweight compatibility shim for legacy SDKs. This ticket focuses on the protocol/state machine, server-side fragment catalog, resume negotiation heuristics, and a small SDK contract update to expose resume tokens and fragment checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes a resume token and fragment catalog per session in the SSE handshake/initial event
Clients can resume mid-stream using resume token + fragment offset, and receive only missing fragments (no duplication at function-call boundaries)
Fragment metadata includes semantic boundary markers to prevent tool/function call replay across reconnects
Compatibility shim implemented: legacy clients receive simplified idempotent tokens and fallback progress markers
Automated integration tests cover reconnect with network jitter, duplicate delivery, and partial fragment arrival
Observability: traces emitted for resume attempts, fragment reconciliation decisions, and chosen fallbacks
tasks: Design state machine for reconnect negotiation and fragment reconciliation (design doc)
Add fragment catalog service in runtime with short-term persistence and eviction
Extend SSE initial event to return resume_token and fragment_window metadata
Implement resume handler that supports resume_token + (fragment_id, offset) semantics
Server-side logic to promote a 'boundary-safe' commit around function-call/structured-output fragments
SDK changes (js/py): expose resume API, automatic reconnection helper, and backward-compatible shim for older SDK versions
Write integration tests that simulate reconnection in the presence of tool/functioncall frames
Add telemetry and dashboards: resume rate, resume success ratio, duplicate fragment rate, mean time-to-resume
discussion_comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Martinez: Initial problem statement added. Noting edge cases where clients reconnect with clock skew and out-of-order fragment arrival.
2026-03-01 - Rohit Singh: Prototype server fragment catalog implemented. Using LRU cache keyed by (session_id, resume_token) with 30s default retention. Observability hooks added.
2026-03-03 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Prioritize function-call boundary safety for tool integrations (high customer impact). Asked for a compatibility path for mobile SDKs.
2026-03-05 - Hannah Lee (Design): Proposed semantic boundary markers within fragment metadata: boundary_type {partial, boundary, final} and function_call_id. See design doc for UX implications.
2026-03-09 - Security (notes): No secret material in tokens; tokens are nonces tied to session+expiry. Recommend rotating nonce scheme before GA.
2026-03-11 - Rohit Singh: Implemented optimistic resume path and experimental 'grace window' to accept near-duplicate fragments and dedupe on function_call_id + sequence.
2026-03-12 - QA: Found flake where resume_token expiry produced full-stream resend for long-poll clients. Working on extending thin-client TTL negotiation.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping fragment retention brief reduces memory but increases chance of full-stream resend for low-traffic sessions. We opted for a tunable TTL per customer tier with default 30s and Dedicated customers allowed to set longer retention. Also scoped a compatibility shim that returns coarse-grained progress marks (sequence number only) for legacy SDKs to avoid protocol churn. Next steps: finish SDK helpers, add robust tests for toolcall dedupe, and schedule an alpha rollout to internal teams.
